text:
Jin: Heads-up — onboarding nova-16k-int4 on staging showed KV checksum drift after ~14k tokens and a few repeated spans. Repro command and short notes below.

Micah: Can you paste the exact invocation and the minimal prompt?

Jin: ./bin/eval --model nova-16k-int4 --context 32768 --quant int4v2 --batch 1 --kv-checksum true --seed 7 --prompt-file tests/long/repro_short.txt
Prompt is ~2k synthetic convo + long instruction to keep looping.

Elaine: Did you try toggling rot_scale? We saw tiny deviations in rotary earlier cause long-run drift.

Jin: rot_scale default 1.0. I tried 1.0002 and it moved onset earlier by ~2k tokens. Log: [2026-03-22T08:11:02Z] idx=14012 kv_checksum=0x3f1a mismatch_detected=true

Devon: Quick checks: (1) run with --disable-kv-cache; (2) dump adjacent KV slots with tools/dump_kv.py; (3) try int8 to see if quant packing is the culprit.

Jin: ran --disable-kv-cache locally — no drift to 20k. That narrows it to cache/pack path.

Micah: I'll kick off a 4-run matrix on ggpu-5: int8, int4 rot=1.0, int4 rot=1.0002, int4 rot=1.0002 shard=single. Will attach diffs.

infra-bot: CI: kv-onboard-bisect/1713055555 queued on ggpu-5 (job 20260322-kv-fuzz).

Elaine: Also add a unit test for pack/unpack idempotence that fuzzes rot_scale and adjacent token indices. If packing differs by a bit for adjacent writes that will accumulate.

Devon: Agreed. I'll audit the int4 packing lanes and the write alignment code; suspect a lane spill when rot offset isn't exact.

Micah: Thanks — Ill post diffs and the sanitized transcript once runs finish.

(ended)
